selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. The Jungfrau Ski Region offers over 200km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels, making it perfect for families with mixed skiing abilities. Rent equipment on-site and take advantage of ski school lessons for younger children.

experiences.name: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure
experiences.description: Embark on a guided family snowshoeing tour across the Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in the Alps. A certified mountain guide leads the group through stunning frozen landscapes, teaching kids about glaciology and alpine ecosystems. Suitable for children aged 6 and up, with all equipment provided.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Visit
experiences.description: Take the iconic cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, known as the Top of Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, visit the Sphinx Observatory, and let the kids play in the snow year-round. The panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier and surrounding peaks are absolutely breathtaking and unforgettable for the whole family.

experiences.name: Swiss Fondue Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss fondue dinner at a cozy alpine chalet restaurant. Families can enjoy classic cheese fondue, raclette, and rösti while learning about Swiss culinary traditions from local hosts. Many restaurants in Zermatt offer family-friendly settings with children's menus and stunning Matterhorn views.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family toboggan runs near Davos. The natural toboggan track stretches over 4km through pine forests and moonlit slopes, offering an exhilarating yet safe adventure for all ages. Evening runs under floodlights add a magical atmosphere, and sleds can be rented at the base station for a budget-friendly winter thrill.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage and take the budget-friendly Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) train toward the Swiss Alps region. Purchase a regional day pass at the airport for savings. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival. Grab a light snack from a nearby convenience store or the hotel reception.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Quick late-night snack from Migros or Coop convenience store near the train station (budget CHF 5-10). Pick up bottled water and breakfast items for the next morning.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel/arrival day. Keep energy conserved for the full week ahead. Swiss trains are punctual and run late into the evening. Validate your ticket before boarding. Exchange currency or use a no-fee travel card for best rates. Pack light snacks for the train ride.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after late arrival. Enjoy a self-prepared breakfast in your room using groceries purchased the night before. After resting, take a short orientation walk around the resort and nearby village to get familiar with the surroundings. Visit the local tourist information office to pick up free maps, ski pass deals, and family discount brochures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest beginner ski slope for a half-day ski session. Rent budget ski equipment from a local rental shop rather than the resort shop to save 20-30%. Look for family ski packages at the local ski school which offer group lessons at reduced rates compared to private instruction. Spend 2-3 hours on gentle beginner and intermediate runs, perfect for getting your ski legs back.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, warm up with hot chocolate, and freshen up. Take a relaxed evening stroll through the alpine village. Browse the local shops and get a feel for the area.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared in room using grocery store items — bread, cheese, yogurt, fruit (budget CHF 5-8 per person)
meals.lunch: Grab a hearty rösti or bratwurst from a mountain hut or ski slope cafeteria — budget option around CHF 12-15 per person
meals.dinner: Dine at a local Gasthaus or traditional Swiss inn in the village. Look for the 'Tagesmenü' (daily menu) which offers a 2-3 course meal at a fixed budget price of CHF 18-25 per person including soup and main course

day_by_day.notes: Buy ski passes for multiple days upfront as multi-day passes offer significant savings. Check if your accommodation includes any ski pass discounts. Children under certain ages often ski free with a paying adult — verify at the ticket office. Rent equipment early in the morning to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing begins early to maximize your ski pass value. Hit the slopes by 9:00 AM when queues are shortest. Focus on intermediate blue runs if you are comfortable, or continue on beginner greens with the family. Take a ski lesson with the group ski school — family group lessons are significantly cheaper than private and are great for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch on the mountain, explore different lifts and runs on the ski area. Try a new sector of the mountain. Families with younger children can enjoy the dedicated kids' ski garden area where instructors supervise children in a fun, safe environment. Take a break mid-afternoon for hot drinks and a rest before the final runs of the day.
day_by_day.evening: After skiing, visit the resort's outdoor ice rink if available — a great budget-friendly family activity. Many alpine resorts offer free or low-cost ice skating in the early evening. Warm up afterward with a fondue dinner — look for budget fondue restaurants in the village where you can share a pot as a family.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared in room — oats, fruit, Swiss muesli from Migros grocery store (budget CHF 4-6 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from the hotel — sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, thermos of hot soup (budget CHF 3-5 per person, prepared the night before)
meals.dinner: Budget fondue dinner at a local restaurant — share a cheese fondue pot as a family. Look for set menus around CHF 20-28 per person including bread and a non-alcoholic drink

day_by_day.notes: Packing your own lunch is the single biggest money-saver on the slopes. Mountain restaurant prices are very high. A thermos of hot soup or tea saves significantly over buying hot drinks on the mountain. Apply sunscreen even on cloudy days — alpine UV reflection off snow is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Take a break from skiing and experience the thrilling Fläsch Toboggan Run near Davos — one of Switzerland's most exciting family toboggan runs. Travel by regional train or PostBus (budget-friendly public transport) to the Davos area. The natural toboggan run is a fantastic family activity suitable for all ages and skill levels. Rent toboggans at the base for a reasonable hourly rate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue tobogganing through the afternoon — most families do multiple runs as the experience is exhilarating and the queues are shorter on weekday afternoons. Explore the Davos area briefly, visiting the lakeside promenade if weather permits. Davos is one of the largest alpine resorts in Europe and has interesting architecture and shops to browse without spending money.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train or PostBus to your resort. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel. Visit the resort's common areas or lounge. If the resort has a sauna or wellness area, check if it is included in your stay — a perfect way to soothe tired muscles after days of winter sports.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared in room — Swiss bread rolls, cold cuts, cheese, orange juice (budget CHF 5-7 per person)
meals.lunch: Buy a warm pretzel or Landjäger (Swiss dried sausage) and a hot drink from a mountain kiosk near the toboggan run (budget CHF 8-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hotel kitchen if available, or visit a local Coop or Migros supermarket for a budget ready meal or ingredients for pasta. Many Swiss supermarkets have hot food counters (budget CHF 8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch Toboggan Run is a highlight of any Swiss Alps family trip. Check opening times and conditions before departure. Wear waterproof outerwear as tobogganing gets wet and snowy. Swiss public transport is excellent — purchase a regional day pass for unlimited travel on buses and trains in the area, which is great value for day trips.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the ski slopes for another full day of skiing. By now the family should be more confident on skis. Try slightly more challenging runs or explore a different sector of the ski area. Take the gondola to a higher elevation for panoramic alpine views — even non-skiers in the family can enjoy the scenic ride and views from the top restaurant terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Participate in a family ski race or fun competition if the ski school is running one — these are often free or very low cost and great fun for children. Alternatively, try snowshoeing as a budget-friendly alternative winter activity. Snowshoe rental is inexpensive and guided snowshoe tours through quiet alpine forests are a magical experience for families.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local event — Friday evenings in Swiss alpine villages often feature live folk music, torchlight descents by ski instructors, or village markets. Check the local tourism office notice board for free events. Enjoy a raclette dinner — another classic Swiss dish where cheese is melted and served over potatoes, pickles, and onions.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared in room — yogurt, granola, banana, Swiss hot chocolate (budget CHF 4-6 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the mountain — wraps, fruit, chocolate, thermos of tea (budget CHF 3-5 per person)
meals.dinner: Raclette dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — look for fixed price Friday dinner menus around CHF 22-30 per person. Some restaurants offer all-you-can-eat raclette which is excellent value for hungry families

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings are lively in Swiss alpine resorts. The torchlight ski descent by instructors is a spectacular free show — check the ski school schedule. If budget is tight, supermarket raclette kits are available for self-catering in the room at a fraction of the restaurant cost. Children's menus at restaurants are typically half price.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely morning with a guided free walking tour of the alpine village — many Swiss mountain villages offer self-guided heritage walks with free printed maps from the tourist office. Visit a local church, historic buildings, and learn about Swiss alpine culture. Stop at a local bakery for fresh-baked bread and pastries — a budget-friendly Swiss breakfast treat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby frozen lake or winter walking trail for a family snowshoe hike or winter walk. Many alpine areas have free or very low-cost marked winter walking paths that are maintained and safe for families. Bring a packed picnic and enjoy a scenic outdoor lunch surrounded by snow-covered mountains. In the late afternoon, return to the slopes for a final ski session if energy allows — late afternoon skiing on Saturdays can be quieter.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate evening of your trip with a special budget-friendly dinner. Visit a local restaurant and order the Tagesmenü — the daily set menu which always represents the best value. Share a bottle of local Swiss wine or order local Swiss beer. Reflect on the week's adventures as a family.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries and bread from a local alpine bakery — croissants, Gipfeli (Swiss croissant), and coffee or hot chocolate (budget CHF 6-9 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic on the winter walking trail — sandwiches, Swiss chocolate, fruit, thermos of soup (budget CHF 4-6 per person)
meals.dinner: Tagesmenü at a local Gasthaus — 3-course set menu including soup, main (often Zürcher Geschnetzeltes or Rösti), and dessert for CHF 22-28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically the changeover day in Swiss resorts so slopes and lifts may be less crowded in the afternoon as weekly renters depart. This is a great time for a final ski session. Visit the Migros or Coop supermarket to pick up Swiss chocolates, cheese, and local specialties as affordable gifts and souvenirs — far cheaper than tourist shops.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Wake up early for one last look at the stunning mountain scenery. Take a short sunrise walk or snowshoe through the quiet village before other tourists are awake — the golden alpine glow on snow-covered peaks is an unforgettable sight. Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, storing luggage at reception if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final activity such as a scenic gondola or cable car ride for panoramic farewell views of the Alps. Visit the local market if it is open on Sunday — Swiss village markets offer local produce, cheeses, and crafts at reasonable prices. Head to the train station and take the Swiss Federal Railways back to Zurich Airport, enjoying the spectacular alpine scenery on the journey.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport with ample time before departure. Enjoy a final Swiss meal at the airport — Zurich Airport has several mid-range dining options. Pick up any last-minute Swiss chocolate from Duty Free as affordable gifts. Depart with wonderful memories of a budget-friendly Swiss Alps family adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final self-prepared room breakfast using remaining groceries — keep it simple with bread, cheese, fruit, and hot drinks (budget CHF 4-6 per person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the train station or a takeaway sandwich and drink from a Coop or Migros station outlet (budget CHF 8-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport — look for the Coop restaurant or Marché Mövenpick which offer good value compared to premium airport restaurants (budget CHF 15-22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Swiss trains to Zurich Airport are direct and very reliable — allow at least 3 hours before your flight for travel, check-in, and security. Swiss Federal Railways luggage forwarding service (Fly Luggage) allows you to check bags directly from major train stations to your airline, saving hassle at the airport. Buy Swiss chocolate at Migros or Coop in the airport departures area — it is significantly cheaper than dedicated chocolate shops. Total estimated budget for the week excluding flights and accommodation: CHF 80-120 per adult per day covering meals, ski passes, equipment rental, transport, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Late arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange transfer or rental car to Swiss Alps. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your Beachfront suite. Grab a light snack from the hotel's 24-hour service or vending area before resting.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A - In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack from hotel room service or hotel lobby café upon arrival. Budget CHF 20–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 22:30, so no activities are scheduled for Day 1. Allow approximately 2–2.5 hours for luggage collection, customs, and transfer to the resort. Pre-arrange airport transfer or rental car in advance to avoid delays. Confirm hotel check-in details ahead of time for a smooth late-night arrival. Prioritize rest for an active Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast to recover from travel. After breakfast, head to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for a first morning of skiing. Rent ski equipment at the resort or nearby ski shop if not already arranged. Begin with beginner-to-intermediate runs in Grindelwald to warm up and assess snow conditions. Ski instructors are available for family members who need lessons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing across the interconnected Jungfrau slopes. More confident skiers can explore the runs toward Wengen, while younger or beginner family members can enjoy the gentler blue runs. Take a mid-afternoon hot chocolate break at one of the mountain huts on the slope.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Head out for a traditional Swiss Fondue Dinner Experience at a cozy alpine chalet restaurant nearby. Warm up with classic cheese fondue, crusty bread, and a glass of local white wine or apple juice for the kids.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Budget CHF 20–30 per person (or included with stay).
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a mountain restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — try rösti, soup, or a hearty sandwich. Budget CHF 25–40 per person.
meals.dinner: Swiss Fondue Dinner Experience at an alpine chalet restaurant. Budget CHF 45–65 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Jungfrau ski pass in advance online for potential discounts. Families with children under 9 often ski free with a paying adult on the Jungfrau region passes. Dress in warm, waterproof layers. Sunscreen is essential even in winter due to high-altitude UV exposure.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on the iconic Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Visit. Take the cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Kleine Scheidegg up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters. Explore the Ice Palace, walk along the glacier plateau, and enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier and surrounding peaks. The Sphinx Observatory and interactive science exhibits are great for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend more time exploring Jungfraujoch — try the snow fun area with snow tubing and short sledding for kids. Have lunch at the top before descending back to the valley by mid-afternoon. Once back in Grindelwald, take a relaxed stroll through the charming village and browse local shops for Swiss souvenirs and chocolates.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rest. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the resort village — try a hearty Swiss mountain meal such as Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce) or Älplermagronen (alpine macaroni).

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant or self-service café at Jungfraujoch. Budget CHF 30–50 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local alpine restaurant in the village. Budget CHF 40–60 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in peak February season. Departure time from Grindelwald should be no later than 9:00 AM to maximize time at the top. Altitude sickness can affect some visitors at 3,454m — take it slow and stay hydrated. Bring warm gloves, hats, and goggles as conditions at the summit can be extreme.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the Aletsch Glacier for a Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure. Join a guided family snowshoeing tour across the largest glacier in the Alps. The guide will provide all necessary equipment including snowshoes and poles. The tour is suitable for families and offers stunning views of the glacier landscape and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoeing tour through the afternoon, exploring different sections of the glacier. The guide will share fascinating facts about the glacier's history and the effects of climate change. Return to the base by mid-afternoon. Warm up at a nearby café with hot drinks and cake.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or take transport back toward the resort area. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby casual dining spot. Try Swiss classics like raclette or a warm bowl of Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup).

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the snowshoeing tour operator, or stop at a mountain refuge hut along the route. Budget CHF 15–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or casual village eatery. Budget CHF 35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure is a guided tour — book in advance through the hotel concierge or a local activity operator. Minimum age for children is typically 6–8 years. Wear warm, waterproof boots and layered clothing. The tour duration is approximately 4–5 hours including breaks. This is a moderate-activity day, perfect mid-trip balance between skiing and sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for a full day of skiing. With a couple of days of skiing already under your belt, the family can now explore more varied terrain. Confident skiers can tackle the red runs between Wengen and Mürren, while beginners continue to build confidence on the blue slopes. Consider booking a group ski lesson for the kids in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mürren area — a car-free village perched dramatically on a cliff with stunning Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau views. Ski down to Mürren for a late lunch and explore the village on foot before taking the cable car back up to continue skiing until late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at a slope-side bar for a warm Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate. Return to the hotel and enjoy a special family dinner at a nicer restaurant — try a three-course Swiss menu with local seasonal ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant in Mürren village — try local cheese dishes and hearty mountain fare. Budget CHF 30–45 per person.
meals.dinner: Nicer alpine restaurant for a sit-down three-course dinner. Budget CHF 55–80 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mürren is only accessible by cable car or train — no cars allowed. The village has a magical, quiet atmosphere perfect for a mid-trip family treat. Check ski pass validity for the Mürren area as it may require an upgrade or is included in the Jungfrau Top Ski Region pass. Ski rentals can be returned and exchanged at most major rental shops across the region.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, travel toward the Davos area for the Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run — one of Switzerland's most thrilling family toboggan experiences. The natural toboggan run near Davos offers an exhilarating ride through snowy forest trails. Sleds are available for rental at the start of the run. This is a fantastic family activity for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy multiple runs down the toboggan track throughout the afternoon. Take a break mid-afternoon at the base hut for hot drinks and snacks. After tobogganing, explore the Davos area briefly — Davos is a lively resort town with shops, cafés, and a scenic frozen lake that may offer ice skating.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a relaxed final full evening with a farewell dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant. Celebrate the trip with a special Swiss dessert such as Meringues with double cream or chocolate fondue for the family.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the toboggan run base hut or a casual Davos café — hearty soups, sandwiches, and Swiss pastries. Budget CHF 20–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality local alpine restaurant. Budget CHF 50–75 per person including dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch toboggan run near Davos is a natural run — conditions depend on snowfall and grooming. Check availability and opening status in advance. Davos is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the Jungfrau region depending on your exact resort location — plan travel time accordingly. Helmets are recommended for tobogganing, especially for young children, and can be rented at the site.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Pack up and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If time allows before departure, take a short scenic walk around the resort area or nearby village to soak in the last views of the Swiss Alps. Pick up last-minute Swiss chocolates, cheese, or souvenirs from local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the transfer back toward Zurich Airport or your onward destination. The drive from the Swiss Alps to Zurich takes approximately 2–3 hours depending on your exact location and traffic. Stop at a roadside or town restaurant for a final Swiss lunch en route.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport with ample time for check-in, security, and departure. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, snowshoeing, glacier exploration, tobogganing, and Swiss alpine culture.

meals.breakfast: Final buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort (check-out meal included or budgeted at CHF 20–30 per person).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a roadside restaurant or town café en route to the airport. Try a final Swiss sandwich, soup, or Birchermüesli. Budget CHF 20–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport — wide range of options from casual to sit-down restaurants. Budget CHF 30–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the drive to Zurich plus check-in and security. Return any rental ski equipment before checking out of the resort area. Zurich Airport has excellent dining and shopping options airside. Declare any food items such as cheese when traveling internationally. Consider purchasing travel insurance for the ski activities if not already arranged.

Take advantage of the alpine wellness facilities — heated indoor pool, sauna, and steam room — to recover from jet lag and acclimatize to the altitude. Concierge briefing on the week's activities and equipment rental arrangements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for an introductory ski session on the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald. Arrange a private ski instructor for all family members to assess skill levels and warm up on beginner-to-intermediate runs. Enjoy the stunning panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. Premium ski equipment rental from the resort's partner ski shop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing pre-dinner drink at the alpine lounge bar. Enjoy a curated selection of Swiss wines and craft cocktails with mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Grand buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant — featuring freshly baked Swiss breads, artisan cheeses, cold cuts, eggs to order, fresh juices, and Swiss bircher muesli.
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Restaurant Grindelwaldblick — a premium mountain restaurant accessible by gondola, offering panoramic views and a menu of hearty alpine cuisine including venison stew, truffle pasta, and fondue.
meals.dinner: Swiss Fondue Dinner Experience at a cozy alpine chalet restaurant near Grindelwald — enjoy traditional cheese fondue, raclette, and meat fondue with premium Swiss wines in a warm, candlelit setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructors at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Ensure all family members have appropriate ski gear and layered clothing. Altitude adjustment may cause mild fatigue — stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Skiing on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — begin with a morning session on the Wengen slopes, known for their wide, well-groomed runs ideal for all skill levels. Take the Männlichen gondola for breathtaking ridge-top views and access to varied terrain. Private ski guide accompanies the family for personalized coaching and route selection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing in the Mürren area — one of Switzerland's most scenic car-free villages perched on a cliff. Access via cable car and enjoy intermediate-to-advanced runs with dramatic views of the Schilthorn. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain hut for hot chocolate and apple strudel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a premium spa treatment — book couples or family massages, alpine herbal baths, and hydrotherapy sessions at the resort wellness center.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — eggs Benedict with smoked trout, freshly squeezed orange juice, croissants, and Swiss honey.
meals.lunch: Luncheon at Restaurant Allmend in Wengen — a refined alpine dining experience featuring seasonal local ingredients, including wild mushroom risotto, grilled alpine beef, and freshly made pasta.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's signature restaurant — a 5-course tasting menu featuring modern Swiss-French cuisine with wine pairing, including dishes such as pan-seared lake trout, truffle risotto, alpine herb-crusted lamb, and artisan Swiss chocolate desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Mürren is accessible only by cable car and train — no cars allowed. Allow extra travel time. The resort concierge can arrange private transfers to the cable car stations. Book evening spa treatments in advance as slots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Visit — depart early morning to make the most of the iconic cogwheel train journey to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters. Board the Jungfrau Railway from Grindelwald or Kleine Scheidegg for the spectacular ascent through tunnels carved into the Eiger. Arrive at the Top of Europe and explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and Snow Fun Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — enjoy snow activities on the plateau including a guided snowshoe walk, a husky sled experience (if available), and panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier stretching 23km below. Visit the Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven shop and the interactive alpine museum. Begin descent in the mid-afternoon to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski experience in Grindelwald village — stroll the charming alpine village, visit artisan shops, and enjoy a warm drink at a traditional Swiss café before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort — packed and prompt to ensure timely departure for Jungfraujoch.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Bollywood or Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — unique dining at 3,454m elevation, offering European and international cuisine with the most extraordinary mountain backdrop in Switzerland.
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at Restaurant Steinbock in Grindelwald — a Michelin-recognized alpine restaurant offering refined Swiss cuisine with locally sourced ingredients, including Bernese highland beef, seasonal vegetables, and artisan desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch visits require advance ticket booking — premium 'Good Morning' tickets offer discounted early access and fewer crowds. Dress in extra warm layers as temperatures at 3,454m can drop to -15°C or below. Children must be monitored closely at high altitude. Carry sunscreen as UV radiation is intensified at elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure — embark on a private guided family snowshoeing tour across the Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in the Alps. Depart from the resort with a certified mountain guide and traverse breathtaking icy landscapes, frozen crevasses, and snow-covered moraines. The guide provides educational commentary on glaciology and alpine ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the snowshoeing tour, enjoy a relaxed afternoon at leisure. Return to the resort and allow younger family members to enjoy the resort's dedicated kids' club with supervised winter activities, snow sculpting, and indoor games. Adults may enjoy the resort's private spa lounge, heated outdoor jacuzzi with mountain views, or a personal training session.
day_by_day.evening: Family movie night or game night at the resort — the concierge can arrange a private screening room with Swiss snacks, hot chocolate, and popcorn for a cozy alpine evening together.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast at the resort — bircher muesli, warm pretzels, Appenzeller cheese, cold cuts, soft-boiled eggs, and freshly brewed coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the glacier — the resort's chef prepares a gourmet packed lunch including artisan sandwiches, thermoses of hot soup, Swiss chocolate, dried fruits, and warm beverages to enjoy amid the glacier scenery.
meals.dinner: In-resort private dining experience — arrange a customized family dinner in a private dining room or igloo-style outdoor setup (if available), with a dedicated chef preparing a multi-course Swiss alpine menu by request.

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoeing on the Aletsch Glacier requires a certified guide — never venture without professional accompaniment. Appropriate footwear and gaiters are provided by the tour operator. Children aged 6 and above are generally suitable for beginner snowshoeing tours. Check with the guide service for age and fitness requirements.

day_by_day.morning: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run — experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family toboggan runs, offering an exhilarating natural track through alpine forest and open snowfields. The resort arranges private transfers to the toboggan area. Enjoy multiple runs with the family, with experienced guides available for first-timers and younger children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from tobogganing and enjoy a final premium ski session on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — choose your favorite runs from earlier in the week and ski with newfound confidence. Take time to enjoy the mountain scenery and capture photos at scenic viewpoints. Optional: book a helicopter scenic flight over the Alps for a once-in-a-lifetime aerial perspective (subject to weather and availability).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell celebration dinner — the resort arranges a special premium dining experience to celebrate the family's alpine adventure. Dress elegantly for a memorable final dinner.

meals.breakfast: Champagne brunch at the resort — a lavish spread including freshly shucked oysters, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, pastries, eggs to order, fresh fruit, and a selection of Swiss and French sparkling wines.
meals.lunch: Après-ski lunch at a mountain terrace restaurant — enjoy the sunshine and mountain views with a menu of grilled meats, alpine salads, warm soups, and Swiss craft beers or mulled wine.
meals.dinner: Gala farewell dinner at the resort's rooftop restaurant or private dining suite — a 7-course chef's tasting menu with Swiss and international wine pairing, featuring seasonal alpine ingredients, handmade chocolates, and a personalized dessert celebrating the family's trip.

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter scenic flight must be booked well in advance and is subject to weather conditions — confirm with the concierge on Day 4 or 5. Tobogganing is suitable for all ages with appropriate safety gear provided. Saturday slopes may be busier — depart for skiing early in the afternoon to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the resort and take a last stroll through the alpine village or resort grounds. Visit the resort gift shop for premium Swiss souvenirs including Lindt chocolates, Swiss watches, alpine herbal products, and handcrafted wooden keepsakes. Optional: a final dip in the resort's heated outdoor pool with mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Private chauffeur arranged by the resort for transfer to the airport or railway station. Ensure all ski equipment rentals are returned and resort charges are settled. Allow ample time for the journey to the airport given alpine road conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — board return flight. Reflect on an extraordinary week of world-class skiing, glacier adventures, and unforgettable alpine luxury in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte farewell breakfast at the resort — order your favorites from the week, including Swiss pastries, eggs Benedict, fresh fruit platters, and premium coffee or tea service.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or en route to the airport — the concierge can arrange a premium packed lunch or recommend a refined café near the departure terminal.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or onboard dining (business/first class) — the resort concierge can coordinate with the airline to arrange special meal preferences or champagne service for the return journey.

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 11:00–12:00 — confirm with the resort in advance and request a late check-out if needed (subject to availability). Ensure passports, ski passes, and all valuables are packed the night before. The resort concierge can assist with luggage shipping if needed. Keep travel documents and flight information easily accessible for departure day.
